svg.title: How GitHub comes to know every workflow of a new repository
svg.desc: GitHub starts a workflow only once it has registered it, and the first push of a new repository may register none; a run registers its workflow, so those that only a schedule, a release or a person starts stay unknown. After its push, python3 .github/blueprint.py create asks GitHub for up to a minute whether it knows every workflow of .github/workflows/. For each that it doesn't, create runs python3 .github/blueprint.py workflows register, which opens a pull request of one commit that GitHub signs, with a comment at the end of each such workflow. Its merge is a push that changes them, which registers them. Run again, the command opens the pull request that takes the comments out, and the files are the blueprint's again. Then every workflow starts on its push, its schedule, its release or by hand.
